recall_prompt: Say how you would find this — what angle the base is, what De Moivre gives for the fifth powers, and what their difference is.
insider_note: Read √3/2 and 1/2 as cos π/6 and sin π/6 and the question is two lines. Two errors cost the marks: taking the angle as π/3, which is the other way round, and making sin(5π/6) negative — it is +1/2, so the answer is i.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the base as cis π/6 and raise to 5
steps.margin_note: First mark. √3/2 = cos π/6 and 1/2 = sin π/6, so both brackets are cis(±π/6) with modulus 1. De Moivre multiplies the angle by 5, giving cos 5π/6 ± i sin 5π/6.
lines: √3/2 + i/2 = cos π/6 + i sin π/6

recall.must_convey: That √3/2 + i/2 is cos π/6 + i sin π/6, so the fifth powers are cos 5π/6 ± i sin 5π/6 by De Moivre.
accept: root three by two plus i by two is cis pi by six, so its fifth power is cis five pi by six and the conjugate gives cos five pi by six minus i sin five pi by six
recognise cos pi by six and sin pi by six, then De Moivre multiplies the angle by five
the base is cis pi by six and the power five gives five pi by six
root three by two i by two ante cis pi by six, De Moivre tho five pi by six
both brackets become cis plus or minus five pi by six

steps.why: √3/2 and 1/2 are cos π/6 and sin π/6, so both brackets are already cis(±π/6) with modulus 1. De Moivre multiplies the angle by 5; nothing else changes.
common_mistakes: Not recognising √3/2 and 1/2 as cos π/6 and sin π/6, and expanding by the binomial theorem.
Taking the angle as π/3 (cos π/3 = 1/2, the other way round).
Writing the second bracket's power with + i sin.

steps.label: Subtract and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Subtracting a number from its conjugate leaves 2i times the imaginary part: 2i sin(5π/6). sin(5π/6) = sin(π/6) = 1/2, so the value is i.

recall.must_convey: That the reduced expression is evaluated to i.
accept: evaluate the reduced form and get i
simplify the powers of omega and the value is i

common_mistakes: Taking sin(5π/6) = −1/2; the sine is positive in the second quadrant.
